statement: Let n = len(s). The function returns a result r (it does not fail) and r = true exactly when there exists an integer d such that 1 <= d < n, n mod d = 0, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, s[i] = s[i mod d]. Equivalently, the non-empty prefix of s of length d occurs n/d >= 2 times consecutively.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 1 <= len(s) <= 10000, and every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97..122).

statement: Let n = len(s). The function does not fail: evaluation returns Result.ok r for some Bool r. In particular, no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 1 <= len(s) <= 10000, and every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase English letter (code 97..122).

statement: Suppose s and t have the same equality pattern: for all i,j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, s[i] = s[j] if and only if t[i] = t[j]. Whenever the function returns Result.ok r_s on s and Result.ok r_t on t, we have r_s = r_t.
preconditions: s and t are byte slices, each with length between 1 and 10000 inclusive and every byte an ASCII lowercase English letter, and len(s)=len(t)=n.
